reasons: Cited Section 20 fully supports the compliant status: 20.1 provides a Vendor defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims covering Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel, with no adverse carve-outs.

20.2 captures the remaining preferred triggers (Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access/disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, Vendor's gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, plus bodily injury and property damage).

20.4 supplies standard indemnity procedure (notice with material-prejudice qualifier, cooperation at indemnitor's expense, control of defence, settlement consent), and 20.5 adds procure/modify/replace/terminate-and-refund remedies expressly in addition to the defence obligation.

Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow (unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized; Customer's violation of Applicable Law) with Vendor Technology/modification/combination/instruction carve-outs, so direction of burden is correct.

21.3 places indemnification obligations, IP infringement and gross negligence/wilful misconduct within Excluded Claims, so Vendor's indemnity is uncapped — better than the fallback super-cap; the rationale's reliance on this is accurate.
No redline or counterparty comment is proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding, and the deterministic check confirms the Vendor IP indemnity is present.
